risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Major customer Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited has set up its own Lead smelter and started operations, and will ramp up capacity in a phased manner, reducing its offtake from the Company.
- Sourcing domestic feedstock has become significantly more challenging due to an influx of new battery recyclers entering the Indian market, coupled with a limited supply of end-of-life EV batteries and domestic plant scrap since major regional gigafactories are not yet fully operational.
- MoEF&CC has classified black mass, an intermediate recycling product, as hazardous waste, requiring separate DGFT export licenses that the government is currently withholding, so the Company can no longer export black mass.
- The Company suspended windmill operations following expiration of its power purchase agreement with Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Limited.
- Progress of the hydrometallurgy forward-integration facility depends on obtaining an amended EPR certification (upgrade from R2 to R4) and passing audits by EV OEMs and Lithium-ion battery manufacturers to secure the supply pipeline.
- The incumbent statutory auditor's two-term tenure expires at the 42nd AGM; a new firm (M/s M. Bhaskara Rao & Co) is proposed for appointment, a transition that carries continuity/handover risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Pursuing forward integration in battery recycling through the hydrometallurgy plant to source black mass from third-party mechanical pre-processors and utilise own material, mitigating raw material shortages.
- Exploring other customers in domestic and international markets to offset reduced offtake from Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited.
- Pursuing LME (London Metal Exchange) membership to sell metal directly to an LME-registered warehouse and boost international visibility.
- Applying for an import license to secure reliable overseas battery scrap sources to address domestic feedstock supply …
